svg.text: SIMPLE SEARCH — INDEX → POSTINGS → TF-IDF, WITH REAL NUMBERS
the title words are counted TWICE
when they repeat in content → 7 tokens
TOKENIZE — text.toLowerCase().split("\W+"), count into a Map
docTermFreq — Map<docId, Map<term, tf>> (the FORWARD index; makes delete cheap)
D1 → { java:2, guide:1, threads:1, and:1, locks:1 }
D2 → { java:1, design:2, patterns:2, in:1, practice:1 }
D3 → { go:2, concurrency:1, channels:1, and:1, goroutines:1 }
NO stop-word removal, NO stemming: "and", "in" are indexed; "pattern" would NOT match "patterns".
THE INVERTED INDEX — postings: Map<term, Map<docId, tf>>
posting list — every doc containing it, with its term frequency
a stop-word that earned a posting list
… guide, threads, locks, in, practice, go, concurrency, channels, goroutines — 13 terms in all
The inner map is docId → tf, not just a Set: the SAME structure answers "who has it" and "how often" ✓
removeDocument reads docTermFreq[docId] to know exactly which lists to touch ⇒ O(terms in doc) ✓
Three maps, no invariant guard — they stay in sync only because ONE synchronized method writes all three.
1. tokenizeQuery("java patterns") → ["java", "patterns"] same tokenizer as indexing — this matters
3. candidates = UNION = { D1, D2 } ← OR semantics. D3 is never scored, never touched.
This is the whole win: 2 map lookups instead of scanning 3 (or 3 million) documents ✓
lookup() returns a defensive COPY of the keySet on every call — fine at 3 docs, a real allocation cost at scale.
tf = count / docLength idf = ln( (N+1) / (df+1) ) + 1 score = Σ tf × idf
patterns: tf missing ⇒ term skipped entirely (no penalty, no zero term)
D2 wins on BOTH counts: it hits both query terms, and its rarer term "patterns" carries 1.3× the idf of "java" ✓
Dividing by docLength stops a long document from winning just by being long ✓
df is recomputed as index.lookup(term).size() INSIDE the per-doc loop ⇒ O(candidates × terms) redundant set copies.
Docs scoring exactly 0.0 are dropped, so a candidate can be in the union and still never appear.
SORT DESC, THEN PAGE — subList(offset, offset+limit)
SearchResult carries the whole Document, so the caller renders the hit without touching the index again.
Pagination happens AFTER a full sort of every candidate — deep offsets still pay for the whole list.
index a doc: O(T) tokens · remove: O(distinct terms in doc) · lookup a term: O(1) + copy
search: O(Σ postings) to build candidates + O(C × Q) to score + O(C log C) to sort
C = candidate docs, Q = query terms. Nothing here is O(total documents) — that is the point of inverting.
Missing vs a real engine: AND/phrase queries, positions, field boosts, stemming, stop-words, snippets, skip lists.

g.text: THE ONE LINE TO SAY OUT LOUD
"A forward index answers what is in this document. Search asks the opposite question, so I invert it:
term → docs. I keep the term frequency in the posting itself so ranking needs no second structure, and I keep
a forward map per doc purely so deletes stay cheap. Scoring is a Strategy — TF-IDF today, BM25 tomorrow,
